items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: with Bucky and John — Bucky Pizzarelli and John Bunch, the group that got called New York Swing, that’s really a remarkable group to be in

ctx.x: It’s almost a whole job in itself to do that kind of thing. But you seem to have been very successful in finding a number of niches in the world of music.

Yes, I think so. I mean I’ve got record companies who still sell all six of my CDs now, I’m still talking to all the presidents of them, and the records are still on the market, and they still sell. And I’ve got deals coming up in the future, just some other stuff, and of course with Bucky and John — Bucky Pizzarelli and John Bunch, the group that got called New York Swing, that’s really a remarkable group to be in, I like this group very much, just piano, bass and guitar. And it’s a very interesting combination…
Yeah. I just, to me there’s nothing like that chunking — what do they call it — hollow body —
